rows.claim: Council approved a $1,500,080 purchase of M500 in-car video systems and Video Manager from Motorola Solutions, Inc. under Sourcewell contract 010720-WCH.
rows.display_copy: $1,500,080 - M500 In-Car Video System and Video Manager
rows.source_document: Resolution / Roll Call 23-1629, Agenda Item 32
rows.page_or_row: p. 1 of the 25-page clerk's file, operative clause 1
rows.source_excerpt: The purchase of M500 In-Car Video System and Video Manager from Motorola Solutions, Inc. in the amount of $1,500,080.00 and per the terms and pricing of the Sourcewell Master Agreement Contract #010720-WCH for use by the Police Department, is hereby approved.
rows.caveat: Read from a scan of a handwritten-annotated page; the printed body text was additionally verified visually.
rows.what_it_does_not_establish: It does not establish what components the approved total contained; the resolution names no line items.

rows.claim: The resolution authorized the Mayor to execute the Short Form Agreement and Addendum already on file with the City Clerk.
rows.display_copy: “the Short Form Agreement and Addendum on file with the City Clerk”
rows.source_document: Resolution / Roll Call 23-1629
rows.source_excerpt: The Mayor is authorized and directed to execute the Short Form Agreement and Addendum on file with the City Clerk, supplementing Sourcewell Master Agreement Contract #010720-WCH with term specific to the City's procurement, on behalf of the City.
rows.caveat: The clause uses the singular “Addendum”; four addenda were executed. Whether “Addendum” was intended collectively is not determinable from the record.
rows.what_it_does_not_establish: It does not establish which documents were physically before council members, or that any member read them.

rows.claim: The resolution recites a competitive-bid determination and the cooperative-purchasing exemption.
rows.display_copy: “have been competitively bid and are available from Motorola Solutions, Inc.”
rows.source_document: Resolution / Roll Call 23-1629
rows.source_excerpt: WHEREAS, the Procurement Administrator has determined that the requested M500 In-Car Video System and Video Manager have been competitively bid and are available from Motorola Solutions, Inc. … using the Sourcewell Master Agreement Contract #010720-WCH
rows.caveat: The recital is accurate as to the cooperative vehicle. The plate-reader component of the price list was added to that vehicle administratively in September 2021, about 19 months after award, without a further solicitation.
rows.what_it_does_not_establish: It does not establish that the plate-reader component itself was competitively solicited.

rows.claim: The council communication described the purchase as upgraded in-car video systems with installation, implementation and video evidence management software.
rows.display_copy: “upgraded in-car video systems with installation, implementation, and video evidence management software”
rows.source_document: Council Communication No. 23-519, submitted by Dana Wingert, Chief of Police
rows.page_or_row: pp. 3-4 of the 25-page file, agenda heading
rows.source_excerpt: Approving the proposition to authorize and enter into a purchase agreement in the principal amount not-to-exceed $1,500,080 for the purpose of purchasing upgraded in-car video systems with installation, implementation, and video evidence management software from Motorola Solutions Inc. … utilizing the Sourcewell Contract.
rows.caveat: This is the council-facing description. It is accurate as far as it goes: the M500 is an in-car video system and VideoManager EL is video evidence management software.
rows.what_it_does_not_establish: It does not establish that the description was complete, nor that anything was withheld.

rows.claim: The synopsis describes camera replacement and body-worn integration and does not mention plate reading.
rows.display_copy: “replace all current devices with new enhanced cameras for high resolution video”
rows.source_document: Council Communication No. 23-519
rows.source_excerpt: Approval of the purchase of upgraded in-car video systems with installation and evidence video management software for the Police Department. This purchase would replace all current devices with new enhanced cameras for high resolution video. The video evidence management software will assist with the integration of body worn camera video and automate the uploading of the video file from the field to improve time efficiency.
rows.what_it_does_not_establish: It does not establish the absence of plate-reader capability in the equipment; the plate-reader lines appear in the ordering document.

rows.claim: The fiscal-impact block and the resolution recital cite different fiscal years and different funding sources, and refer to a debt financing agreement not found in the record.
rows.display_copy: “The debt financing agreement includes the five (5)-year extended service and warranty agreement.”
rows.source_document: Council Communication No. 23-519
rows.page_or_row: p. 3, FISCAL IMPACT and ADDITIONAL INFORMATION
rows.source_excerpt: Fiscal Year (FY) 2023 $470,480 FY2024 $257,400 FY2025 $257,400 FY2026 $257,400 FY2027 $257,400 — Funding Source: Adopted Operating Budget, FY2023, Page 209 … The debt financing agreement includes the five (5)-year extended service and warranty agreement.
rows.caveat: The resolution recites “FY 2024 Adopted Operating Budget, General Fund”; PO 24209, issued the next day, labels the same dollar pattern FY24-FY28. The dollar amounts agree; the year labels are offset by one.
rows.what_it_does_not_establish: No debt-financing instrument for this purchase appears in the reviewed records. Not found is not the same as nonexistent.

rows.claim: The council communication lists one previous council action: the 2016 WatchGuard in-car and body-camera award.
rows.display_copy: Previous council action listed: RC 16-1638 (September 26, 2016)
rows.source_document: Council Communication No. 23-519
rows.source_excerpt: Date: September 26, 2016 — Roll Call Number: 16-1638 — Action: Proposal for an in-car camera and body camera solution and related software and implementation services from Watchguard Video. (Council Communication No. 16-533)
rows.what_it_does_not_establish: It does not establish that no other related procurement existed; the Chain B instruments of July-September 2023 are not listed and no council action for them appears in the reviewed records.

rows.claim: Neither the resolution nor Council Communication 23-519 mentions ALPR, LPR, license plates, Vigilant, LEARN, PlateSearch, VehicleManager, hot lists, retention or data sharing.
rows.display_copy: 0 occurrences on pages 1-4
rows.source_document: Roll Call 23-1629 clerk's file, pp. 1-4
rows.source_excerpt: Full-page OCR of pages 1-4 yields no occurrence of ALPR, LPR, license plate, Vigilant, LEARN, PlateSearch, VehicleManager, hot list, retention or data sharing. Pages 1 and 3 were additionally inspected visually at 130 dpi.
rows.caveat: This is a statement about the resolution and the council communication, not about the 25-page file. The attachments in the file do contain these terms.
rows.what_it_does_not_establish: It does not establish concealment, intent or that anything was withheld.

rows.claim: Item 32 was adopted as part of a consent agenda covering items 3 through 38 on a single roll call.
rows.display_copy: Consent agenda, items 3 through 38, one roll call, 7-0
rows.source_document: Des Moines City Council agenda and roll call RC 23-1597, meeting of November 20, 2023
rows.source_excerpt: APPROVING CONSENT AGENDA - items 3 through 38 … Motion Carried 7-0
rows.caveat: The agenda footnote describes consent items as routine items enacted by one roll call vote without separate discussion.
rows.what_it_does_not_establish: It does not establish what any individual council member read, knew, understood or intended. That is outside the record and outside this exhibit.

rows.claim: The clerk's roll-call file as produced runs to 25 pages and contains no quote, no line items and no pricing breakdown.
rows.display_copy: 25 pages: resolution (1-2), council communication (3-4), W24-152 (5-6), Mobile Video Addendum (7-13), Subscription Software Addendum (14-18), EPSLA (19-23), Equipment Purchase Amendment (24-25)
rows.source_document: Roll Call 23-1629 clerk's file, produced by the City on August 4, 2026
rows.source_excerpt: Pages fully accounted for: 1 resolution; 2 roll-call vote sheet; 3-4 Council Communication 23-519; 5-6 Short Form Agreement W24-152; 7-13 Mobile Video Addendum; 14-18 Subscription Software Addendum; 19-23 Equipment Purchase and Software License Addendum; 24-25 Equipment Purchase Amendment.
rows.caveat: This is the City Clerk's roll-call file as produced in August 2026. It is not a certified reproduction of the agenda packet distributed before the meeting. Two documents in it bear post-vote dates: the Equipment Purchase Amendment is dated November 22 and carries a City signature reading November 21.
rows.what_it_does_not_establish: It does not establish that these attachments were physically before council members on November 20, 2023.

rows.claim: The Mobile Video Addendum provides that the City may share its plate-reader data with other similarly situated law-enforcement agencies by selecting the option inside Vigilant VehicleManager.
rows.display_copy: “Customer, at its option, may share its LPR data … by selecting this option within Vigilant VehicleManager.”
rows.source_document: Mobile Video Addendum, §4.5 License Plate Recognition Data
rows.source_excerpt: License plate recognition (“LPR”) data collected by Customer is considered Customer Data (as defined in the Master Agreement) and is therefore subject to the Customer's own retention policy. Customer, at its option, may share its LPR data with other similarly situated Law Enforcement Agencies (“LEAs”) which contract with Motorola to access Vigilant VehicleManager by selecting this option within Vigilant VehicleManager. Other similarly situated LEAs may similarly opt to share their LPR data with Customer using Vigilant VehicleManager.
rows.caveat: The 25-page file is the City Clerk's roll-call file as produced in August 2026. Whether these pages were before council members on November 20, 2023 is not established.
rows.what_it_does_not_establish: It does not establish that any sharing relationship existed in 2023, or when any relationship was later configured.

rows.claim: The same clause restricts logins, not sharing: the City must ensure no user logins are given to officers of other agencies without the vendor's written consent.
rows.display_copy: “no user logins are provided to agents or officers of other local, state, or Federal LEAs without the express written consent of Vigilant”
rows.source_document: Mobile Video Addendum, §4.5
rows.source_excerpt: Only individuals who are agents and/or sworn officers of Customer and who are authorized by Customer to access Vigilant VehicleManager on behalf of Customer through login credentials provided by Customer (“User Eligibility Requirements”) may access Vigilant VehicleManager … Customer will ensure no user logins are provided to agents or officers of other local, state, or Federal LEAs without the express written consent of Vigilant.
rows.caveat: This restricts credentials, not detection sharing. The two are different mechanisms and must not be conflated.
rows.what_it_does_not_establish: It does not restrict which agencies may appear as sharing counterparties. An agency with its own vendor contract can be a configured counterparty without holding a Des Moines login.

rows.claim: The addendum treats commercial plate-recognition data as a conditional future step requiring a separate Data License Addendum, and equates LEARN with Vigilant VehicleManager.
rows.display_copy: “If Customer purchases a subscription to commercial license plate recognition data, then Customer will execute … Data License Addendum.”
rows.source_document: Mobile Video Addendum, §4.4 Vigilant Access
rows.source_excerpt: Customer may opt for subscription to additional Subscription Software, including use of the Law Enforcement Archival Network (“Vigilant VehicleManager”), which is subject to the terms and conditions of the SSA and the Vigilant Addendum when agreed to in writing by the parties. If Customer purchases a subscription to commercial license plate recognition data, then Customer will execute and agree to the terms of Motorola's standard Data License Addendum.
rows.caveat: The City had already contracted for commercial national vehicle-location data under a separate agreement executed in July-August 2023. That earlier contract is not in this file.
rows.what_it_does_not_establish: It does not establish that commercial data was purchased under this chain. The plate-reader licence purchased under this chain is defined by the vendor's own price file as agency data only.

rows.claim: The vendor determines the storage location of cloud-hosted content in its sole discretion, subject to a United States location commitment for US customers.
rows.display_copy: “Motorola will determine, in its sole discretion, the location of the stored content”
rows.source_document: Mobile Video Addendum, §7.1 Data Storage
rows.source_excerpt: Motorola will determine, in its sole discretion, the location of the stored content for cloud hosted software Products. All data, replications, and backups will be stored at a location in the United States for Customers in the United States.
rows.caveat: In the clerk's roll-call file as produced in August 2026. Whether these pages were before council members on 20 November 2023 is not established.
rows.what_it_does_not_establish: Where the data is in fact stored has not been independently verified.

rows.claim: The only audit right in the executed agreements runs from the vendor to the City: a licence true-up of credentialed user counts.
rows.display_copy: “Motorola will have the right to conduct an audit of total user licenses credentialed by Customer”
rows.source_document: Subscription Software Addendum, §4.1 License True-Up
rows.source_excerpt: Motorola will have the right to conduct an audit of total user licenses credentialed by Customer for any Subscription Software during a Subscription Term, and Customer will cooperate with such audit.
rows.caveat: No City-side audit, inspection or log-access right appears anywhere in the executed instruments reviewed. Not found is not the same as nonexistent.
rows.what_it_does_not_establish: It does not establish that the City lacks any other route to platform records; it establishes only that the reviewed agreements contain no such right.

rows.claim: The City agreed that sub-processors, and their sub-processors, may process Customer Data under their own terms.
rows.display_copy: “sub-processors, who in turn may engage additional sub-processors to process personal data and other Customer Data”
rows.source_document: Subscription Software Addendum, §2.2 End User Licenses
rows.source_excerpt: Motorola may use, engage, resell, or otherwise interface with third-party software, hardware or services providers … and other sub-processors, who in turn may engage additional sub-processors to process personal data and other Customer Data. Customer agrees that such third-party software or services providers, sub-processors or their respective sub-processors may process and use personal and other Customer Data in accordance with and subject to their own respective licenses or terms and in accordance with applicable law.
rows.caveat: The clause governs “Customer Data.” Under Mobile Video Addendum §4.5, City-collected plate data is Customer Data. State the chain; do not shorten it.
rows.what_it_does_not_establish: It does not establish that any sub-processor exists, is named, or has processed Des Moines plate data. No list, flow-down or notification obligation appears in the agreement.

rows.claim: The City negotiated a right to terminate on 30 days' notice if changes in Iowa law make the equipment substantially unusable by law enforcement.
rows.display_copy: “in the event the Equipment become substantially unusable by law enforcement due to changes in law in the state of Iowa”
rows.source_document: Equipment Purchase and Software License Addendum, §4.3 Customer Termination
rows.source_excerpt: In addition to the termination provisions of the Master Agreement, the Customer may terminate this Addendum with 30 days notice to Motorola in the event the Equipment become substantially unusable by law enforcement due to changes in law in the state of Iowa. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer remains responsible for all fees and invoices associated with all Equipment delivered prior to the date of termination.
rows.caveat: A City-favourable clause. Report it alongside the vendor-favourable ones.
rows.what_it_does_not_establish: It does not establish that the right has ever been exercised or considered.

rows.claim: The order-of-precedence clause in the City's own short form points to an EPSLA and a Software License Addendum executed on or around September 29, 2023.
rows.display_copy: “executed by City and Contractor on or around September 29, 2023”
rows.source_document: Short Form Agreement, Contract No. W24-152, §1 Scope of Services; Orders
rows.source_excerpt: the order of preference shall be as follows: 1) City Short-Form Agreement, 2) Sourcewell Contract #010720-WCH, 3) Equipment Purchase and Software License Addendum (EPSLA) agreed upon and executed by City and Contractor on or around September 29, 2023 and Software License Addendum (SLA) agreed upon and executed by City and Contractor on or around September 29, 2023, and 4) Contractor's Quotes.
rows.caveat: The Motorola-party EPSLA produced bears the date November 20, 2023. The only instrument in the record executed on September 29, 2023 belongs to the separate Vigilant / H-GAC chain. No executed Software License Addendum has been produced for either chain. The most economical reading is a drafting carry-over from the City's earlier Vigilant short form, prepared by the same buyer.
rows.what_it_does_not_establish: It does not establish deliberate incorporation of the other chain's terms. That reading is untested and is not adopted here.

rows.source_document: Motorola QUOTE-2241626, “Updated M500 VaaS”
rows.caveat: Every one of the 130 in-car systems shipped with a component the vendor's own pack list calls an “M500 ALPR DVR.” The $67,580 is the licence-and-support layer, not the extent of the plate-reader deployment.
rows.what_it_does_not_establish: It does not establish that plate-reader capability was 4.5% of the purchase in any operational sense.

rows.claim: A solution-description page from the same quote describes the M500's plate-recognition capability and its integration with the Vigilant LEARN platform.
rows.display_copy: “carefully integrated with our market-leading Vigilant LEARN LPR platform”
rows.source_document: Motorola quote solution-description page, produced separately by the City as “Info about purchase”
rows.source_excerpt: The M500 has powerful License Plate Recognition (LPR) capabilities, and is carefully integrated with our market-leading Vigilant LEARN LPR platform … reads plates in up to three lanes of traffic simultaneously, while moving at up to 70mph … hotlists can be agency-owned or shared … the market-leading Vigilant PlateSearch application … Optionally, you can extend this to include LPR data from neighboring agencies and commercial customers.
rows.caveat: This is vendor marketing language in a vendor document. Attribute it to the quote literature, not to the City.
rows.what_it_does_not_establish: It does not establish what the City bought. The SKU actually purchased is defined by the vendor's price file as agency data only.

rows.claim: The vendor's own Sourcewell price file defines the purchased SKU as CarDetector Mobile with Vigilant PlateSearch, agency data only.
rows.display_copy: DDN3421A · “CarDetector Mobile, Vigilant PlateSearch (agency data only)”
rows.source_document: Motorola (fka WatchGuard) Sourcewell price file, effective June 2022, “In-Car Video (ICV) & License Plate Reader (LPR) Systems”
rows.source_excerpt: DDN3421A  M500 Basic ALPR VaaS — CarDetector Mobile, Vigilant PlateSearch (agency data only), includes 90-day IDP trial. $516/yr/vehicle.
rows.caveat: This is the sentence that keeps the story accurate: the council-approved purchase did not include commercial national vehicle-location data.
rows.what_it_does_not_establish: It does not describe the separate commercial-data contract, which sits on a different cooperative vehicle.

rows.claim: The delivery pack list records an “M500 ALPR DVR” component for every one of the 130 systems.
rows.display_copy: 130 systems delivered, each with an “M500 ALPR DVR” line
rows.source_document: Motorola pack list, SO 30718107 / Delivery 77429598, PO 24209

rows.caveat: The DVR SKU is branded “M500 ALPR DVR” for every unit. This is hardware naming, not a separate licence.
rows.what_it_does_not_establish: It does not establish that plate reading was enabled on any given unit, or when.

rows.claim: The Sourcewell solicitation behind contract 010720-WCH contains no reference to license plates, license-plate recognition, LPR or ALPR.
rows.display_copy: RFP #010720 · “Public Safety Video Surveillance Solutions” · 0 plate-reader references
rows.source_document: Sourcewell RFP #010720, public notice November 7, 2019; proposals due January 7, 2020
rows.source_excerpt: Scope: “Public Safety Video Surveillance Solutions with Related Equipment, Software and Accessories.” Verified by full-text search: the only four case-insensitive matches for “plate” in the document are the word “template.”
rows.what_it_does_not_establish: It does not establish that adding plate readers later was improper. The change-request mechanism is expressly authorised by the contract.

rows.claim: Plate readers were added to the cooperative price list on September 14, 2021 by a two-page vendor change request.
rows.display_copy: “WatchGuard Video mistakenly left off a key component of our VaaS offering – The License Plate Reader (LPR). It is now included in the VaaS price list.”
rows.source_document: Sourcewell Price and Product Change Request, contract 010720, effective September 14, 2021
rows.source_excerpt: WatchGuard Video mistakenly left off a key component of our VaaS offering – The License Plate Reader (LPR). It is now included in the VaaS price list.
rows.caveat: Under Article 4 of the contract, an executed change form becomes an amendment incorporated by reference. The cooperative's own rule is that modifications must be within the scope of the original solicitation. Whether any scope determination was made is not found in the records produced.
rows.what_it_does_not_establish: It does not establish intent, evasion or wrongdoing by any party. The document says what it says.

rows.claim: Five change forms for contract 010720-WCH were identified in 2021.
rows.source_document: Sourcewell production, five Price and Product Change Request forms for contract 010720

rows.caveat: The September 3, 2021 form created the VaaS price list that the September 14 form says the plate reader was left off of. That form's signature is dated “8/31/22” - an anomaly on the face of the document, noted and not built on.
rows.what_it_does_not_establish: It does not establish a sequence of intent. Earlier RDP working notes described only two forms; five is the corrected count.

rows.claim: The City stated that it does not generate or keep copies of ALPR database search logs.
rows.display_copy: “search logs are not something the City generates or keeps copies of”
rows.source_document: City of Des Moines response to an open records request dated October 1, 2025, sent December 10, 2025
rows.source_excerpt: 6. ALPR database search logs — The City has no documents responsive to this request. The searches are queried as needed, and search logs are not something the City generates or keeps copies of. 7. ALPR database audit reports or trails — All documents responsive to this request are considered Intelligence Data and are deemed confidential pursuant to Iowa Code Section 692.8. Spot audits are conducted in response to complaints or allegations of misuse. Only one entry exists from a review of searches to ensure case numbers were being documented and it is attached.

rows.claim: The clause making City-collected plate data “Customer Data” points to a definition that is not in either document the addendum identifies as the Master Agreement.
rows.display_copy: “Customer Data (as defined in the Master Agreement)” — not defined there
rows.source_document: Mobile Video Addendum §4.5; Short Form Agreement W24-152; Sourcewell contract 010720-WCH; Motorola Solutions Customer Agreement (version NA MCA v2.0, 5 September 2024)
rows.page_or_row: MVA §4.5; definitions across the named instruments
rows.source_excerpt: The Mobile Video Addendum defines “Master Agreement” as Sourcewell 010720-WCH plus W24-152. Neither of those documents contains a definition of “Customer Data.” The Motorola Solutions Customer Agreement in the record does not define the term inside itself either: it states the term has the meaning given to it in the Data Processing Addendum, which is hosted at a motorolasolutions.com URL “as updated, supplemented, or superseded from time to time” and which provides that in a conflict the DPA will prevail.
rows.caveat: Do not say “Customer Data is defined in the MCA.” The MCA refers onward to a vendor-hosted Data Processing Addendum. Further, the only MCA edition in the record is dated September 5, 2024 and post-dates the November 2023 order; W24-152 §3 voids in-product terms on presentation, and whether that reaches a URL-hosted addendum is unresolved.
rows.what_it_does_not_establish: It does not establish that the City's plate data is unprotected, nor what the November 2023 definition said. This is a gap in the produced record and an unresolved definitional chain, not a finding about ownership.
